channel.title: n8n release notes: editor and nodes
channel.description: Feature-level updates from n8n releases: what shipped in the editor and the integration nodes.

item.title: Databricks Node: Enable the Job resource
item.description: The Databricks node now exposes a Job resource in its resource selector, enabling four previously hidden operations: Run, Get Job, Get Run, and Get Run Output. These operations and their logic already existed in the node but were not selectable in the UI; this change makes them visible and usable in workflows targeting Databricks jobs.

item.title: Supabase Node: Add OAuth credentials and reuse them for MCP
item.description: The Supabase node now supports OAuth2 authentication alongside existing API key credentials. When using OAuth2, you select a Supabase project and n8n automatically manages a dedicated Data API secret key, reusing it across runs and refreshing it if it becomes invalid. Node parameter order was updated to show Resource and Operation first. Supabase OAuth2 credentials can also be used to enable the Supabase MCP server in the AI Assistant tools list.

item.title: Show migration progress on report overview
item.description: The Migration report in Settings now shows a progress bar at the top, displaying the share of workflows compatible with the target version along with a "{compatible} of {total} compatible" label. Workflow counts throughout the report are now formatted with locale-aware number formatting for better readability. The bar is also accessible, with proper progressbar roles and ARIA attributes.

item.title: Crypto Node: Add RSA-OAEP hash option
item.description: The Crypto node's asymmetric encrypt/decrypt operations now let you choose the RSA-OAEP hash algorithm, supporting SHA-256 (default, preserving existing workflow behavior) or SHA-1. This enables interoperability with systems that require SHA-1 for OAEP padding when encrypting or decrypting with RSA keys.

item.title: Tell the AI Assistant which preview tabs are open
item.description: The AI Assistant now only sees the preview tabs you currently have open, including which one is active, instead of every artifact ever produced in the thread. Closing tabs is reflected to the assistant, so it won't reference artifacts you've closed unless you explicitly ask about them. This gives more accurate, up-to-date context without affecting prompt caching.

item.title: Release Browser Use to all users
item.description: Browser Use in the n8n Assistant is now available to all users, controlled by the instance admin setting N8N_INSTANCE_AI_BROWSER_USE_ENABLED (on by default) rather than an experiment. It remains unavailable on phones and tablets, including iPads in desktop mode. The experimental "Set up automatically" credential setup option is now disabled by default for all users, with its underlying code kept in place for a possible future return.

item.title: Open any project resource as an AI Assistant tab
item.description: In the AI Assistant, you can now open a new tab for any workflow, data table, or agent in the thread's project directly from a preview tab bar. A new tab button opens a searchable menu scoped to the thread's project, listing recently edited resources (already-open ones are filtered out) or search results. Picking a resource opens it as the active tab, and the choice is saved across reloads.

item.title: Close AI Assistant tabs and keep the open tabs per thread
item.description: You can now close preview tabs in the AI Assistant. Each tab shows a close button on hover or focus, and middle-click or Delete also close a tab. Closing the active tab selects the next (or previous) tab, and closing the last tab closes the preview. Open tabs, closed artifacts, and the active tab are now saved per thread, so they're restored when you reopen it. Closed artifacts reopen automatically if referenced again from chat or the artifacts list.

item.title: Azure OpenAI Chat Model Node: Add the deployment dropdown
item.description: The Azure OpenAI Chat Model node now lets you pick a deployment from a dropdown list instead of typing its name, avoiding typos that previously caused a DeploymentNotFound error. New nodes default to version 1.1, offering 'From List' and 'By ID' modes. The list requires an Azure AI Foundry credential with a Project set; classic credentials or empty projects show a clear error message. Existing version 1 nodes keep their text field and saved values unchanged.

item.title: Show the trigger icon on the execute button and run a trigger from its menu
item.description: The canvas Execute button has been redesigned: it now simply reads "Execute" and shows the selected trigger's icon instead of a second "from <trigger>" line, with the trigger name still shown in a tooltip. Choosing a trigger from the dropdown now immediately runs the workflow and sets it as the default trigger. The button is now a consistent height, so adjacent Stop buttons no longer resize. The Builder chat uses the same updated component.

item.title: Hide generated AI tools listed in NODES_EXCLUDE and empty node creator entries
item.description: NODES_EXCLUDE now lets you hide a generated AI tool variant (e.g. microsoftOutlookTool) without removing its base node. Additionally, the node creator panel now hides subcategories or views (like 'Other AI Nodes' or 'Other ways...') that have no browsable nodes left, based on NODES_INCLUDE/NODES_EXCLUDE settings, keeping the panel cleaner for restricted instances.

item.title: Replace severity with impact categories in the migration report
item.description: The migration report now shows clearer impact labels instead of low/medium/critical severities: Upgrade blocked, Executions fail, Behavior changes, and Capability removed. Each breaking-change rule has been reclassified based on its actual runtime effect, with color-coded badges and tooltips explaining each category. Rules are now sorted by severity of impact, with blockers shown first and removed capabilities last, making it easier to prioritize fixes before upgrading.

item.title: Add keyboard controls to n8n Assistant panel
item.description: You can now open and close the n8n Assistant panel in the Agent builder using Cmd+J (macOS) or Ctrl+J (Windows/Linux). Escape also closes the panel when focus is inside its input, and the close button now shows an Escape hint. Other canvas shortcuts remain disabled while typing in inputs.

item.title: Show Gateway credits promotions on community nodes
item.description: n8n now displays Gateway credits promotions for eligible community nodes, shown as a callout in the node creator, the NDV, and the credential modal. The promotion text is sourced dynamically and only appears while Gateway credits support the node and the current time falls within the promotion's active window, disappearing automatically once it expires.

item.title: Group the node credential picker by where each credential comes from
item.description: The node credential picker now groups credentials by where they come from, showing personal credentials under 'Available to you' and project or instance-shared credentials under headings like 'Available in <project>' or 'Available to everyone'. Empty groups are hidden and search filtering respects the groups. This is only active when granular credential sharing (N8N_ENV_FEAT_CRED_SHARING) is enabled; otherwise the dropdown looks unchanged.

item.title: Suggest Gateway credit services during node discovery
item.description: The AI assistant's node suggestion feature now also surfaces relevant n8n Connect Gateway credit services, such as Firecrawl, PDF.co, Brave Search, and LlamaParse, when recommending nodes by category. Previously these services were only found via search or list actions. This applies to assistant chat, workflow building, and agent building, helping users discover credential-free options for web search, scraping, and document parsing.

item.title: Restyle AI Assistant tab bar and add a tab hover card
item.description: Redesigned the AI Assistant's preview tab bar with an updated look, and added a hover card for each tab. The card shows the tab's full name, and for workflows also displays the last edited time and a Published/Draft status, while data table tabs show the edited time and column count. Details load efficiently via batched requests and refresh in the background. Closing tabs and the new tab button are not yet included.

item.title: Azure OpenAI Chat Model Node: Rename to Azure AI Foundry Chat Model
item.description: The 'Azure OpenAI Chat Model' node has been renamed to 'Azure AI Foundry Chat Model' to better reflect that it supports the full Azure AI Foundry catalogue (including Llama, Mistral, Cohere, DeepSeek, Grok and Claude models), not just OpenAI models. Existing workflows are unaffected, and searching for 'Azure OpenAI' still finds the node thanks to a new alias.

item.title: Improve Agent Builder intro interactions
item.description: The Agent Builder intro's template list has been refined: rows now use accessible, semantic markup with keyboard support (Tab, Enter, Space), a hover-revealed arrow indicator, subtle staged fade-and-blur animation, and cleaner spacing and text sizing. Redundant action buttons were removed since rows themselves are now clickable, improving usability for both mouse and keyboard/screen-reader users.

item.title: Group canvas toolbar buttons in a single container
item.description: The canvas toolbar buttons—zoom controls (bottom-left) and canvas actions (top-right)—are now grouped into a single visual container with a shared background, rounded corners, and shadow, instead of appearing as separate floating buttons. This saves canvas space and gives a cleaner, more unified look in both the editor and the node creator panel, in light and dark mode.

item.title: Add adaptive comment input to the review activity feed
item.description: The comment input in workflow review activity feeds now sits directly after the last entry and adapts its height as you type, growing from one line to multiple. It stays sticky at the bottom, keeps focus and drafts intact when the feed loads or errors, auto-scrolls new content into view, and fades in newly received comments for a smoother review experience.

item.title: Revamp the Agent skills modal
item.description: The Agent skills modal has been revamped: it now opens with a file/folder upload option and a manual entry option, supports drag-and-drop, and opens imported skills directly in the editor with their references. Leaving via Back discards unsaved manual drafts. The editor now follows a new field order, with existing validation and telemetry preserved.

item.title: Animate height changes in the MCP callback URLs dialog
item.description: The Allowed callback URLs dialog under Settings → Instance-level MCP now animates smoothly instead of jumping. Switching between 'All callback URLs' and 'Only trusted URLs', adding or removing a URL row, and validation messages appearing all transition with a smooth grow/shrink motion. Reduced motion settings are respected, showing a simple fade instead. No functional or validation behavior changes.

item.title: Preview own connected clients on the MCP settings overview
item.description: The instance-level MCP settings overview now previews your first three connected clients directly, showing brand, client type, connection time, and access summary, with a hover-revealed revoke action. A 'View all' row appears only when more clients exist. The clients page's owner column is now more compact and the revoke button is properly right-aligned.

item.title: Add queued message controls to agent Preview chat
item.description: Agent Preview chat now lets you send new messages while an agent is running or waiting for approval. Pending messages queue up visibly, can be edited or removed before they start, and are restored after a page reload. Each queued message joins the conversation once its execution begins. Stop now only cancels the current run, leaving queued messages intact, and works across multi-main setups.

item.title: Displays instance admins (and owner) in all project user lists
item.description: Project member lists now always show instance owners and admins with a 'full access' role and explanatory tooltip, since they already have implicit access to all projects. They can't be removed or edited, and are excluded from the user picker when adding members. Related API endpoints now reject edits/removals of instance admins and ignore them in add requests. Also adds pagination and search to project member lists.

item.title: Azure OpenAI Chat Model Node: Add the project input and the deployment list call
item.description: Internal groundwork was added to the Azure OpenAI Chat Model node to support Azure AI Foundry projects, including a new project input and backend logic to list a project's chat-capable deployments for both API-key and Entra ID credentials. This change is not yet user-visible; a follow-up release will add the deployment selection dropdown.

item.title: Create credentials and variables from promotion bindings
item.description: When applying promoted workflow changes, users can now create missing credentials and variables directly from the promotion binding screen, using the existing editors with prefilled names, types, and expressions. Items save into their destination project, creating the project if needed, and bindings resolve once the editor closes. OAuth setup is preserved during save. This feature is currently behind a flag pending resolution of an expression-validation edge case.

item.title: Add expanded N8nMarkdownEditor view
item.description: The Markdown editor used in places like Agent instructions now supports an expanded, full-screen dialog view. Users can toggle between the inline editor and an expanded view via a toolbar button (also available in floating toolbar mode), with editing state and content preserved when expanding, collapsing, or pressing Escape, including in raw Markdown mode.

item.title: Make SSO the primary option on the sign-in page when SSO is enabled
item.description: When SAML or OIDC is the active login method, the sign-in page now leads with a Continue with SSO button, with the email/password form collapsed behind a disclosure (still accessible via a recovery query parameter). If password sign-in is refused because SSO is required, an inline callout with its own SSO action appears instead of a toast. Redirects after login, including on OIDC, now correctly return users to their original destination, with hardened validation against unsafe redirect URLs. Instances without SSO are unaffected.

item.title: Show each policy violation with its scope when a save, publish or execution is refused
item.description: When a workflow save, publish, or manual execution is blocked by a node or credential type policy, the editor now shows a clear toast listing each blocked type and its scope, instead of a generic error. On the open canvas, each blocked type is a link that selects the affected nodes, making it easier to find and fix policy violations.

item.title: Add Mistral Vibe to the MCP connect-client picker
item.description: Instance-level MCP settings now let you connect Mistral Vibe from the "Connect a client" picker, listed under Web alongside ChatGPT. Selecting it opens Vibe's connector marketplace on a preset n8n template; users paste their server URL and complete OAuth consent. Vibe also gets its own brand icon, and connected Vibe clients now show the Mistral logo and assistant type in the connected-clients table instead of a generic icon.

item.title: Databricks Node: Show the Databricks Trigger in the node picker
item.description: The Databricks Trigger node is no longer hidden and now appears in the node picker, making it discoverable when searching for Databricks, as well as the new aliases pipeline, job, and DLT. No functional changes were made to the trigger itself—only its visibility changed, letting users add it directly from the picker instead of needing prior knowledge of the node.

item.title: Add Gateway credits option to Agent web search
item.description: Agents can now pay for web search using Gateway credits, the same way they already can for models and tools. When Brave Search is served through the AI Gateway, the web search credential picker offers a managed "Gateway credits" option with a balance indicator, so no personal Brave API key is needed. This option is not available for SearXNG, which the gateway does not support.

item.title: Microsoft Teams Node: Send activity feed notifications to a user
item.description: The Microsoft Teams node now supports sending activity feed notifications to a user via a new Activity Notification resource with a Send operation. It works with OAuth2, Microsoft, and Service Principal credentials, validates the Topic Link, and surfaces clear errors when the companion Teams app isn't installed or required permissions are missing. Existing OAuth2 credentials must be reconnected to pick up the new scope.

item.title: Use test label and icon for agent preview
item.description: In the AI agent builder, the preview action has been relabeled as "Test agent" with a flask icon replacing the previous play icon, better reflecting its purpose. The close button for the test panel now has an updated accessible label, "Hide test", improving clarity for screen reader users.

item.title: Show a restricted node panel in the NDV with contact-admin and replace paths
item.description: Opening a node blocked by a type availability policy now shows a restricted-node panel in the NDV instead of an editable node, explaining the restriction and offering to contact an instance admin or replace the node while keeping its connections. Input/output panels become read-only and no trigger panel is shown for restricted nodes. This requires the type-availability-policies module and an appropriate license.

item.title: Microsoft Teams Node: Add online meeting attendees on Create, Create or Get and Update
item.description: The Microsoft Teams node's Online Meeting resource now supports Attendees on Create, Create or Get, and Update. Pick people via the shared user picker or supply IDs/emails by expression, with an optional Attendee/Presenter role on Create and Update. Allowed Presenters gains a Specific People option. Update replaces the full attendee list; an empty list clears attendees. Requires User.Read.All permission for lookups.

item.title: Suggest Gateway credits after credential errors
item.description: When testing a credential fails on a node that supports Gateway credits, n8n now shows a callout suggesting to switch to Gateway credits instead. Choosing this option switches the node's credential to Gateway credits, preserves its other credentials, saves the workflow, and confirms with a toast. The callout only appears for supported nodes and credential types, and requires Gateway credits to be licensed and enabled on the instance.

item.title: Add a write lock to the agent builder
item.description: The agent builder now uses a collaborative write lock so only one browser tab can edit an agent at a time. Editing requests the lock on first change; other tabs become read-only with a banner and a take-over option if the same user has it open elsewhere. Idle writers auto-release after 20 seconds, and closed or crashed tabs free the lock via heartbeat and TTL, preventing conflicting edits.

item.title: Anthropic Node: Add prompt caching to the Message operation
item.description: The Anthropic node's Text → Message operation now supports a Prompt Caching option (Disabled, 5 Minutes, or 1 Hour), matching the Anthropic Chat Model sub-node. When enabled, requests include a cache breakpoint so repeated tool-call loops and large system prompts are billed at reduced rates for cached tokens. Reported token usage now correctly includes cache creation and read tokens. Disabled by default, so existing workflows are unaffected.

item.title: Move agent skills to a separate card
item.description: In the AI Agent builder, Skills now appear in their own dedicated card below Model and Instructions, labeled with the subtitle "How this agent handles specific tasks". Previously grouped within the Capabilities section, Skills are now easier to find and manage as a distinct part of agent configuration.

item.title: Show timestamp dividers in the agent preview chat
item.description: The agent preview chat now shows timestamp dividers above messages, so it's clear when a conversation happened. A divider appears above the first user message and again whenever more than an hour passes or the calendar day changes, labeled as "Today at HH:MM", "Yesterday at HH:MM", or a full date, formatted in the viewer's locale. Older history without a saved timestamp simply shows no divider.

item.title: Databricks Node: Show the Chat Model node in the node picker
item.description: The Databricks Chat Model node is now visible in the node picker when adding a Chat Model to AI Agent or Basic LLM Chain nodes. Previously the node existed but was hidden while it was being finalized. Existing workflows already using this node are unaffected.

item.title: Move web search to agent capabilities
item.description: Web search settings for agents have moved from the Advanced settings panel to the Capabilities card, where it now appears as its own capability row. Native provider options (for models like OpenAI and Anthropic) and fallback providers (Brave, SearXNG) with their credential selectors are still available, just relocated for easier discovery when configuring an agent's capabilities.

item.title: Make view related tag permissions available by default
item.description: Custom instance roles now include a 'Tags: View' permission by default, letting all users view and select existing tags on workflows even without tag management rights. Previously this was bundled with 'Manage', requiring extra permissions just to see tags. The tag picker now clearly indicates when a user lacks permission to create new tags. Note: existing custom roles created before this change won't automatically get the new scope.

item.title: Distinguish skills from tools in session timelines
item.description: Agent session timelines now distinguish skill calls from regular tool calls, showing them with a dedicated 'Skill' label, a book icon, and an orange color. Node rows in the timeline also display the actual configured node icon when available. Skill events can be filtered, searched, and inspected in the detail panel showing their input and output, making it easier to trace agent behavior.

item.title: MiniMax Node: Fetch available models from the API instead of a hardcoded list
item.description: The MiniMax and MiniMax Chat Model nodes now fetch available models directly from the MiniMax API instead of relying on a hardcoded list, so new models appear automatically. The Model field (version 1.2) offers a searchable, credential-aware list plus an option to enter a custom model ID. Existing workflows keep their prior node version and static model list unchanged.

item.title: Microsoft Teams Node: Add [@mention](https://github.com/mention) support to message Create
item.description: The Microsoft Teams node now supports @mentions when creating channel or chat messages. Add one or more mentions via a new user picker (search by list, ID, or email), and n8n resolves each user against Microsoft Graph so mentions render as real chips and trigger the recipient's Teams notification, instead of appearing as plain, inert text.

item.title: Mark required agent fields
item.description: The agent editor now marks the Model and Instructions fields with a red asterisk to indicate they are required, matching the convention used elsewhere in n8n forms. This is a copy-only UI update to improve clarity; no functional or validation changes were made.
